images.title: Check 4 with two digits
images.purpose: Show that divisibility by 4 depends only on the last two digits: 8536 ends in 36, and 36 = 4 × 9, so 8536 is divisible by 4.
images.composition: One row of four big digit boxes centred high on a white page, one equation line centred below, wide empty space around.
images.exact_structure: One row of exactly 4 equal square boxes holding 8, 5, 3, 6. The first 2 boxes are plain grey #6B7280 outline. The last 2 boxes (3 and 6) are filled reddish purple #CC79A7. Below the last two boxes, one teal #0072B2 line of text. Exactly 4 boxes, 1 equation line.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
boxes of unequal size, or more or fewer than 4 digit boxes
images.takeaway: Only the last two digits decide divisibility by 4.
images.description: The number 8536 as four boxes with the last two digits 3 and 6 highlighted, and the line 36 = 4 × 9 below.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the two digits that matter and say why 36 tells us about the whole number.

image_decisions.why: The idea that only the last two digits matter is a picture idea; one highlighted digit row carries it.
